people.jesus.relations: Mary is his mother. Mark names four brothers and mentions his sisters.
people.jesus.meaning: John baptizes him in the Jordan. He teaches, heals, and casts out demons in Galilee. He tells his disciples three times that he will be killed and rise. He is crucified, and a young man at the tomb says he has risen.
people.mary-mother.relations: Jesus is her son. People name James, Joses, Judah, and Simon as his brothers.
people.mary-mother.meaning: She comes with Jesus’ brothers and stands outside, calling for him. Jesus says that whoever does God’s will is his family. People in his own country later call him the son of Mary.
people.john-baptizer.relations: King Herod puts him in prison for the sake of Herodias. His disciples bury his body.
people.john-baptizer.meaning: He baptizes in the wilderness and says a mightier one comes after him. He baptizes Jesus in the Jordan. He tells Herod that his marriage is not lawful. Herod has him beheaded to keep an oath made at a supper.
people.peter.relations: Andrew is his brother. Jesus heals his wife’s mother of a fever.
people.peter.meaning: Simon leaves his nets, and Jesus names him Peter. He calls Jesus the Christ, then rebukes him for speaking of death. He says he will not deny Jesus, then denies him three times and weeps. The young man at the tomb sends word to “his disciples and Peter.”
people.mary-magdalene.relations: She goes with Salome and with Mary the mother of James and Joses. Jesus had cast seven demons out of her.
people.mary-magdalene.meaning: She watches the cross from afar and sees where Jesus is laid. She brings spices to the tomb and hears that he has risen. The women flee and say nothing, for they are afraid. Jesus then appears to her first, but the others do not believe her.
places.jerusalem.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem and clears the temple in chapter 11. He is arrested and tried there in chapters 14 and 15.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.jordan.summary: John baptizes the crowds and Jesus in the Jordan in chapter 1. Jesus teaches beyond the Jordan in chapter 10.
places.jordan.limits: The text does not say where on the river John baptized.
places.galilee.summary: Jesus begins to preach in Galilee in chapter 1. In chapter 16 the young man says Jesus goes there ahead of the disciples.
places.galilee.limits: Galilee is a wide region. The marker shows only its general location.
places.tyre.summary: People from around Tyre come to Jesus in chapter 3. In chapter 7 a Greek woman there begs him to help her daughter.
places.tyre.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names only the area around it.
places.sidon.summary: People from around Sidon come to Jesus in chapter 3. Jesus goes into the borders of Tyre and Sidon in chapter 7.
places.sidon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names only the area around it.
places.jericho.summary: Blind Bartimaeus calls out as Jesus leaves Jericho in chapter 10. Jesus gives him sight.
places.jericho.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.olives.summary: Jesus sends two disciples from the Mount of Olives in chapter 11. He warns four disciples there in chapter 13. He goes there after the supper in chapter 14.
places.olives.limits: The marker shows the mount’s general location.
places.nazareth.summary: Jesus comes from Nazareth of Galilee in chapter 1, and John baptizes him.
places.nazareth.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.capernaum.summary: Jesus teaches in the synagogue at Capernaum in chapter 1. Four men lower a paralyzed man through a roof there in chapter 2. In chapter 9 he asks the disciples what they argued about.
places.capernaum.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.caesarea-philippi.summary: In chapter 8 Jesus goes to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way Peter calls him the Christ.
places.caesarea-philippi.limits: The text names only the villages around the town. The marker shows the town.
places.bethany.summary: Jesus goes out to Bethany with the twelve in chapter 11. In chapter 14 a woman pours costly ointment over his head there.
places.bethany.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location. This is not Bethany beyond the Jordan.
places.bethsaida.summary: Jesus sends the disciples ahead by boat toward Bethsaida in chapter 6. In chapter 8 people bring a blind man to him there. Jesus heals him in two steps outside the village.
places.bethsaida.limits: The marker shows the general area. It does not point to one ancient ruin.
places.sea-galilee.summary: Jesus calls four fishermen by the sea of Galilee in chapter 1. He calms a storm on it in chapter 4. He walks on it in chapter 6.
places.sea-galilee.limits: The marker shows the lake. The text gives no exact place for the storm or the crossings.
sources.web.limits: The account supports close reading. The publisher keeps verses 9–20 of chapter sixteen and adds notes about the text.
sources.black-mark.limits: Black gives the reading of the text. Original manuscripts were not examined. Proposed lost-ending explanations are not treated as facts here.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-10.limits: This is selected Church teaching. A chapter named only in the lesson heading is not counted as covered.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-20.limits: This is selected Church teaching. A chapter named only in the lesson heading is not counted as covered.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-27.limits: This is selected Church teaching. A chapter named only in the lesson heading is not counted as covered.
sources.net-nt-map.summary: The map index gives selected city and region points.
sources.net-nt-map.limits: This is a map reference only. It does not prove events, ancient roads, houses, tombs, or the unnamed mountains.
sources.atlas-canaan.summary: This Church-published atlas names towns and regions in Canaan.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Only selected map points come from this atlas. The earlier review record remains unchanged. The atlas does not prove Gospel events or exact routes.
chapters.*.mapNote: The points mark places this chapter names, as settings or in speech. The exact houses, roads, and tombs are not known.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The map shows points, not travel lines. It does not join movements from other Gospels.
